# Disagreement Log — 1 Clement Chapter 22

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 22:1 "confirms all these things" — all agree

- All three agents agree that "faith in Christ confirms all these things." Recorded.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 22:1 "hearken to me" vs. "hear me" vs. "listen to me"

- **EMET:** "hearken to me; I will teach you"
- **LOGOS:** "hear me; I will teach you"
- **PNEUMA:** "listen to me. I will teach you"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 34:11):** *akousate mou* — hear me
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "hear me" (LOGOS). "Hearken" (EMET) is archaic for a Psalm citation that Clement presents as Christ's living voice.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 22:2 "desires life" vs. "desires life" vs. "wants to really live"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "who desires life"
- **PNEUMA:** "Do you want to really live?"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 34:12):** *thelōn zōēn* — desiring life
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "who desires life." PNEUMA's interrogative form is dynamic but SOPHIA retains the indicative as in the LXX.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 22:3 "guile" vs. "deceit" vs. "lies"

- **EMET:** "your lips from speaking guile"
- **LOGOS:** "your lips from speaking deceit"
- **PNEUMA:** "stop letting your mouth spread lies"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 34:13):** *mē lalēsai dolon* — not to speak deceit/guile
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "your lips from speaking guile" (EMET). "Guile" (*dolos*) is a more precise term than "deceit" — it implies deliberate, cunning deception.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 22:4 "Turn away from evil" vs. "Turn aside from evil" vs. "Reject evil"

- **EMET:** "Turn away from evil"
- **LOGOS:** "Turn aside from evil"
- **PNEUMA:** "Reject evil"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 34:14):** *ekklinon apo kakou* — turn aside/away from evil
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "Turn away from evil" (EMET). The verb *ekklinō* = to turn aside from; "turn away" is clear.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 22:4 "seek peace and pursue it" — all agree

- All agents agree. The verb *diōkō* (pursue/chase) applied to peace is striking — peace is something to be actively hunted. Recorded.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 22:5 "cry for help" vs. "supplication" vs. "call out"

- **EMET:** "ears toward their cry for help"
- **LOGOS:** "ears open to their supplication"
- **PNEUMA:** "listens when they call out to him"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 34:15):** *ōta autou eis deēsin autōn* — his ears toward their petition/supplication
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "his ears are open to their cry" (blending EMET and LOGOS). *Deēsis* = petition/supplication/cry.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 22:6 "cut off the remembrance" — all agree

- All agents agree on "cut off the remembrance of them from the earth." Recorded.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 22:7 "troubles" vs. "afflictions" — Ps 34:17

- **EMET:** "from all his troubles"
- **LOGOS:** "from all his afflictions"
- **PNEUMA:** "from all their troubles"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 34:17):** *ek pasōn tōn thlipseōn autou* — from all his tribulations/pressures
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "from all his troubles." *Thlipsis* = tribulation/pressure/trouble; "troubles" is more general than "afflictions" and suits the LXX register.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 22:9 "surround him who hopes" vs. "encircle him" vs. "wrapped in mercy"

- **EMET:** "mercy will surround him who hopes in the Lord"
- **LOGOS:** "mercy shall encircle him who hopes in the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "those who trust in the Lord are wrapped in mercy"
- **Greek (LXX Ps 32:10):** *ton de elpizonta epi kurion eleos kuklosei* — mercy will encircle the one hoping in the Lord
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "mercy shall surround him who hopes in the Lord." "Surround" (EMET) and "encircle" (LOGOS) are synonymous; "surround" is simpler.

---

*End of disagreement log for 1 Clement Chapter 22. This completes the disagreement logs for 1 Clement Chapters 1-22.*
